title: NEC Rail Waterproofing Membrane Repair
description: Enclosed is a Request for Quotations (RFQ) for Rail Waterproofing Membrane Repair. If you would like to submit quotation, follow the instructions in Section J of the solicitation, complete the required portions of the attached document, and submit it to the address shown on the Standard Form 1442 that follows this letter. The U.S. Government intends to award a firm fixed price purchase order (P) to the responsible company submitting an acceptable offer with a LPTA evaluation. The Government may award a contract based on initial quotations without holding discussions; however, we may hold discussions with companies in the competitive range if necessary. The site visit will be held on September 22, 2026 at 10.00am at Sint Michielswarande 40, 1040 Etterbeek. Prospective offerors/quoters should complete the form �19BE2026Q0005 - Site Visit Registration Form� and send it to BrusselsBids@state.gov to arrange access to the site visit. The conference call will be held on September 25, 2026 at 10.00am on Teams. Prospective offerors/quoters should contact BrusselsBids@state.gov to gain access to the Teams call. Questions are to be sent no later than September 30, 2026 at 5.00pm and must be sent to BrusselsBids@state.gov. Quotations are due by October 14, 2026 at 2.00pm. No quotations will be accepted after this time. Proposals must be in English and incomplete proposals will not be accepted. Your quotation must be submitted electronically to BrusselsBids@state.gov. It is important to make sure the submission is made in specific size and format; Adobe Acrobat (pdf) file format. The file size must not exceed 30MB. If the file size should exceed the 30MB, the submission must be made in separate files and attached to separate emails with less than 30MB each. In order for a quotation to be considered, you must also complete and submit the following: Volume I, as detailed in Section J Volume II, as detailed in Section J Offerors shall be registered in the SAM (System for Award Management) database at https://www.sam.gov prior to submittal of their offer/proposal as prescribed under FAR 4.1102. Failure to be registered at time of proposal submission may deem the offeror�s proposal to be considered non-responsible and no further consideration will be given. Therefore, offerors are highly encouraged to register immediately if they are interested in submitting a response to this requirement.

title: IMPLEMENTATION OF THE GEM ACCELERATOR
description: Lahden seutu – Lahti Region Oy, operating under the name Business Lahti, requests tenders for the planning, implementation and operation of the GEM Accelerator. The GEM Accelerator is an international business accelerator focusing on the electrification, automation and digitalisation of mobility, transport and logistics. It is established through the Lahti GEM Supercluster project, funded by the European Regional Development Fund through the Helsinki-Uusimaa Regional Council. The Service includes detailed programme planning, national and international participant scouting, marketing and communications, management of the application and selection processes, implementation of three (3) accelerator batches, participant-specific support, partner and investor engagement, monitoring, reporting and final handover. At least eighteen (18) companies or teams shall be selected for the three batches in total. The Service is intended for Finnish and international startups, growth companies, research-based teams and potential spin-offs that have progressed beyond the initial idea stage. The primary working language of the Service is English. The Service shall be implemented through a hybrid model, with key in-person activities primarily organised in the Lahti region. The Agreement period is seventeen (17) months, from 1 November 2026 to 31 March 2028. The Tenderer shall state a total price for the Service. The total price may not exceed EUR 180,000 excluding VAT and shall include all costs necessary for the performance of the Service. The price will not be scored. Tenders will be compared solely on the basis of quality, with a weight of 100%. One (1) Supplier will be selected. Tenderers may submit a tender individually or as a consortium. The selected Supplier shall be responsible for the performance of the Service in its entirety, including work performed by consortium members and subcontractors. The detailed scope, requirements, minimum suitability requirements, quality evaluation criteria and contractual terms are specified in the invitation to tender and its annexes.

description: Gegenstand der Ausschreibung ist die Gewährung einer anteiligen Darlehensfinanzierung zur Beschaffung von Eisenbahnfahrzeugen mit elektrischem Antrieb für den Einsatz im Schienenpersonennahverkehr ab vsl. Dezember 2027 in sowie von und nach Schleswig-Holstein. Mit dieser Bekanntmachung werden potenzielle Darlehensgeber dazu eingeladen, ihr Interesse für die Teilnahme an dem anstehenden Darlehenswettbewerb zu bekunden. Interessenten, die die geforderten Eignungsnachweise und Erklärungen vorlegen, erhalten Zugriff auf die Vergabeunterlagen, können der Vergabestelle hierzu Änderungen vorschlagen und werden zur Abgabe von Angeboten aufgefordert. Die Vergabestelle behält sich vor, geeignete Unternehmen zur Angebotsabgabe aufzufordern, die sich nicht an diesem Interessenbekundungsverfahren beteiligt haben. Zur Eignungsfeststellung und Teilnahme am weiteren Verfahren werden Interessenten gebeten, auf die Unterlagen im Vergabeportal unter der Adresse https://entera1.de/261_pia zuzugreifen, die dort herunterladbaren Formblätter – soweit erforderlich – auszufüllen, und als Scan oder digital ausgefüllt inkl. eines Nachweises, dass der Interessent über eine Zulassung zur Vergabe von Darlehen in Deutschland verfügt bis zum 14.10.2026, 15:00 Uhr (MEZ) an folgende E-Mail-Adresse zu schicken: kontakt@zugsh.de. Hinweis: Zusätzlich zur Gewährträgerhaftung des Landes Schleswig-Holstein für die ZUG.SH AöR wird für das Darlehen eine Kapitaldienstgarantie des Landes bereitgestellt, um Risiken für den Darlehensgeber zu reduzieren und möglichst günstige Zinskonditionen für die ZUG.SH zu erreichen. Weitere Informationen können Sie der Leistungsbeschreibung im Vergabeportal entnehmen.

title: Laboratory-Scale Gas Atomizer
description: The National Research Council of Canada (NRC) is seeking the supply, delivery, and installation of a laboratory-scale Gas Atomizer (GA) to enhance powder synthesis activities at the Clean Energy Innovation (CEI) facility in Mississauga. At the CEI-Mississauga facility, the development and production of advanced battery materials is one of the core activities. High-quality, spherical metal and alloy powders are crucial in advancing the research on energy materials. Obtaining powders with precise alloy compositions, particle sizes, morphologies, and quality in small quantities from commercial sources poses significant challenges. To address this issue, NRC intends to procure a GA capable of preparing molten alloys with specific compositions and atomizing them using high-speed gas to produce spherical and fine powders.

title: Basin Dredging, Garnish, NL
description: The scope of work for this project consists of furnishing all labour, plant, equipment, materials, supervision and incidentals required for the Garnish Harbour Dredging Project at Garnish, Newfoundland and Labrador. In general, the work under this contract includes, but is not necessarily limited to, the following: 1. Harbour Dredging Works – Dredging of designated harbour areas to restore navigational depths and improve vessel access. 2. Removal of Underwater Obstructions – Removal and management of sediment, boulders, debris and other underwater obstructions encountered within the dredging limits. 3. Transportation and Disposal of Dredged Material – Loading, hauling and disposal of all dredged material at an approved waste management facility. 4. Marine Survey and Verification Services – Provision of survey and positioning services required to support dredging operations and confirm completion of the work. 5. Environmental Protection and Site Restoration – Implementation of environmental protection measures during construction, followed by site cleanup, restoration and demobilization upon completion of the project. The completion date for all work under this project must be completed 12 weeks after award date. Before submitting a bid, it is recommended that Contractors visit the site and its surroundings, at their own expense and schedule, to review and verify the form, nature and extent of the work, materials necessary for the completion of the works, the means of access to the site (including ferry services), severity, exposure and uncertainty of weather, soil conditions, any accommodations they may require, and in general shall obtain all necessary information as to risks, contingencies and other circumstances which may influence or affect their bid. No allowance shall be made subsequently in this connection on account of error or negligence to properly observe and determine the conditions that will apply. Take all appropriate safety measures for any visit to the site, either before or after acceptance of the bid.

description: TWO PHASE SELECTION PROCESS PHASE 1 - REQUEST FOR QUALIFICATION The scope of work for this project consists of furnishing all labour, plant, equipment, materials, supervision and incidentals required for the Dredging Admirals Beach Small Craft Harbour project at Admirals Beach, Newfoundland and Labrador. In general, the work under this contract includes, but is not necessarily limited to, the following: 1. Harbour Dredging Works – Dredging of the harbour basin and channel to restore navigational depths and improve marine access within the harbour. 2. Removal and Disposal of Dredged Material – Removal, transportation and disposal of dredged sediments, boulders, debris and other dredgable materials at approved upland disposal facilities. 3. Marine Survey and Dredging Control Services – Provision of marine survey services, dredging control and verification activities required to support the dredging operations and confirm completion of the work. 4. Environmental Protection Measures – Implementation and maintenance of environmental protection measures associated with marine construction activities, including measures to control sediment migration, protect fish habitat and prevent pollution of the surrounding marine environment. 5. Marine Operations and Harbour Coordination – Coordination of the work with harbour users and marine traffic, including the management of vessels, floating equipment and construction activities within the harbour environment. The Contractor must perform and complete the Work by March 31st , 2027.

title: Design and Construction of a Modular Office Complex, CFB Edmonton
description: DEFENCE CONSTRUCTION CANADA (DCC) is requesting Proposals from Design-Build Teams to design and construct a new 250-person modular office complex at CFB Edmonton following a modified design-build approach. Additional details are provided in the Request for Proposals (RFP) documents. The estimated construction cost for this opportunity is in the range of $14.8 million. Firms that consider themselves qualified to provide these services are invited to submit their proposals through the MERX Electronic Bidding System on or before the closing date and time indicated on the Electronic Bidding System. This solicitation is being conducted in accordance with the requirements set out in the Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA), Chapter Nineteen of the Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) and the World Trade Organization Agreement on Government Procurement (WTO-GPA). The selected contractor will be required to hold a valid Designated Organization Screening (DOS), issued by the Contract Security Program (CSP) within Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC).  Details concerning the Security Requirements for this project are identified in Amendment No.1 to the RFP documents. Questions regarding this solicitation are to be directed ONLY to the point of contact identified in this advertisement.  Bidders who address their questions to anyone other than the point of contact during the solicitation period may, for that reason alone, be disqualified. Bidders can obtain contract award results from the DCC website at https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/contract-activity. DCC now publicly discloses information on payments made to prime contractors so that subcontractors know when they can expect payment. Information on payments made in the past 90 days on construction contracts over $100,000, as well as further information regarding DCC’s prompt payment commitment, can be obtained from the DCC website title: EW038-270709 - Northern Innovation Centre Conceptual Design Study – RFP
description: Please note that late submissions will not be considered or accepted. Public Works & Government Services Canada (PWGSC) requires the services of an architectural firm (Consultant), acting as the Prime Consultant with a multi-disciplinary team of sub-consultants for the delivery of services required for this project. The facility will be located at the Invuik Satellite Station Facility located in Inuvik, Northwest Territories. The Inuvik Satellite Station Facility (ISSF) is an international, multi-use science and technology facility and is located approximately 200km north of the Arctic Circle. NRCan requires the consultant to investigate options of accommodating their program in a modular building vs typical northern construction. A Class C cost estimate and conceptual schematic options developed through this study to seek early project approval to determine the project’s future viability. NRCan requires Pre-design/ Functional Programming and Schematic services to support preliminary costing and design work for a new multi-use modular facility of approximately 1,277m², excluding supporting areas to be proposed by the Prime Consultant and team. For this project, scope is limited to NRCan program requirements only, with future stakeholder participation or expansion to be considered separately once confirmed. Project stakeholder requirements are outlined within the Terms of Reference. See the Terms of Reference for more details.

title: France – Specialist optical instruments – Réalisation et qualification des blocs optiques X de diagnostics plasma pour le Laser Mégajoule
description: Le marché a pour objet l’analyse de la définition technique fournie par le CEA et la démonstration de l’aptitude de cette définition à atteindre les performances spécifiées ainsi que la réalisation, les contrôles et la qualification d’un bloc optique X (BOX) de diagnostics plasma (imageur X-mous) du LMJ. Ce bloc optique est constitué notamment de deux voies de mesure à double miroir, composées chacune d’un miroir plan et d’un miroir torique, inséré sous vide secondaire. Le périmètre de la prestation est le suivant : - l'étude et la réalisation des sous-ensembles opto-mécanique du BOX comprenant la partie mécanique du bloc optique et la partie optique du bloc optique, - l'intégration et pré-alignement du BOX sur un banc optique visible spécifique à définir par le titulaire, - l'assistance à la qualification du BOX sur générateur X sur site CEA, - les équipements et moyens de manutention et outillages de configuration, - les livraisons documentaire associées. Le marché est découpé en : une part ferme comprenant l’analyse du dossier de définition fournis par le CEA ainsi que les justifications optiques et mécaniques détaillées permettant de démontrer la validation de l’ensemble des performances souhaitées ; une part optionnelle comprenant la réalisation, la recette usine et la qualification sur site du BOX et des moyens de soutien, les approvisionnements des matériaux et matériels nécessaires à sa réalisation ; des parts optionnelles supplémentaires concernant des BOX de conception similaire intégrant également des voies d'imagerie à miroirs X.

title: Netherlands – Interpretation services – Tolkdiensten
description: Om de operationele slagkracht van de ILT te versterken, wordt de inkoop van tolkdiensten gecentraliseerd bij één gecontracteerde partij. Medewerkers van de ILT komen tijdens hun taakuitvoering regelmatig in contact met anderstalige partijen, waarbij accurate communicatie cruciaal is voor een rechtmatige handhaving. De huidige overeenkomst voor tolkdiensten verloopt van rechtswege per 31 december 2026. Dit beschrijvend document legt de basis voor een eenduidige marktbenadering, waarmee de ILT één betrouwbare partner selecteert voor alle ad hoc en geplande tolkbehoeften vanaf 1 januari 2027. De scope van deze aanbesteding omvat het leveren van alle benodigde mondelinge, audiovisuele en fysieke tolkdiensten ten behoeve van de ILT. De opdracht omvat zowel de coördinatie, de logistiek als de daadwerkelijke uitvoering van de tolkdiensten in alle benodigde (gangbare en schaarse) talen. Binnen de scope van de af te sluiten overeenkomst wordt onderscheid gemaakt tussen twee vormen van dienstverlening, te weten: 1. ad hoc tolkdiensten; 2. planbare Tolkdiensten. De omvang zal nabij 104.000euro per jaar bedragen.

PROJECT INFORMATION: Multipurpose Athletic Field � Army Combat Fitness Testing This project utilizes a Design-Build-to-Budget delivery method to design and construct a new facility to contain a 54,600 SF multipurpose athletic field at Fort McCoy, Wisconsin. The facility shall consist of a 200 meter rubberized running track and an artificial turf infield (sized according to Army Techniques Publication (ATP) 7-22.01 Holistic Health and Fitness Training requirements) for completing the annual Army Fitness Testing (AFT). Supporting facilities include site development, modification to existing improvements, utilities and connections, lighting, paving, sidewalks, storm drainage, information systems, landscaping and signage. Consistent temperature control inside the facility shall be provided by self-contained systems. ATFP measures in accordance with the Department of Defense (DoD) Antiterrorism for Buildings will be provided. A life safety analysis of the facility shall be conducted to determine compliance with UFC, IBC, and NFPA codes and standards. A new addressable fire alarm system shall be installed in the facility that is compatible with the existing base fire alarm reporting system. Comprehensive building design services shall be required. Accessibility for individuals with disabilities shall be required. The multipurpose athletic field will be periodically occupied and shall require adequate clearance and circulation for personnel, maintenance and operations. Utility connections and telecommunications system(s)shall be coordinated. The facility shall be designed to a minimum life of 40 years and in accordance with DoD's Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC) 1-200-02 High Performance and Sustainable Building Requirements including energy efficiencies, building envelope, and integrated building systems performance. This is not a continuously used facility, and during periods of non-use utilities will be reduced or disconnected to conserve energy. title: Role Player Support
description: This solicitation is set aside exclusively for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB). The objective of this requirement is to provide realistic role player support services in support of the Naval Special Warfare Command (NSWC) enterprise. These critical role player services include routine unit-level training exercises as well as periodic, short-notice advanced training exercises, both designed to replicate the complex tactical environments and scenarios encountered by Special Operations Forces (SOF). Role player requirements span eight distinct categories, including specialized linguists, tactical opposing forces (OPFOR), amputee role players, and pyrotechnic/weapons subject matter experts. Offerors are strictly required to read all solicitation documents in full to ensure complete proposal submission compliance. Attachment 1 - Performance Work Statement (PWS) contains Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI). Due to strict security and dissemination controls, the PWS is password-protected. Prospective offerors shall email the Contracting Point of Contact, Emily Lonigro, at Emily.Lonigro@socom.mil to obtain the access password. All email requests shall explicitly reference solicitation number H9224026QE075 and shall include the requesting firm's Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) code as well as their SAM Unique Entity ID (UEI). Offerors shall submit written questions during the quote and proposal preparation period utilizing Attachment S-1 - Q&A. All questions shall be received no later than 10:00 AM Eastern Time (ET) on 24 September 2026, as only written questions will receive a formal response. To ensure a timely and precise response from the government, each submitted question shall include the document name, document date, specific page, paragraph, clause, or other definitive citation requiring clarification. Final quotes shall be submitted no later than 10:00 AM Eastern Time (ET) on 14 October 2026. Quotes shall remain valid for no less than 180 days from the date of the RFQ closing.

title: France – Construction work – Construction de 57 logements sociaux et 118 places de stationnement en sous-sol et 4 places de parking en extérieur. « Les prairies du Jura Lot A1 et Le lynx Boréal lot A2 » ZAC du DESSOUS - SERGY (01)
description: Le projet se décompose de la manière suivante : Un îlot A1 composé de 2 bâtiments A11 et A12. Les bâtiments de l'ilot A1 accueillent 27 logements en accession sociale (PSLA). Les logements proposés vont du T2 au T5 duplex et possèdent tous un balcon ou une terrasse. Certains logements en RDC possèdent aussi des jardins privatifs. Le bâtiment A12 est scindé en deux volumes liés par des passerelles et est en R+2+Combles. Le bâtiment A11 est en R+1+Comble. Le local vélo en RDC est situé en limite de propriété. L'accès piéton à l'ilot A1 s'effectue via l'espace public par une rampe partagée avec les véhicules. Un parking de 4 places (dont une place PMR) se trouve au cœur de l'ilot A1. Un parking, mutualisé entre l'ilot A1 et l'ilot A2, de 118 places se trouve en sous-sol. L'entrée du parking se situe sur l'îlot A1, en limite avec l'îlot A2. Un îlot A2 composé de 3 bâtiments : les bâtiments A21, A22 et A23. Les bâtiments de l'ilot A2 se composent de 30 logements locatifs sociaux. Les logements proposés vont du T2 au T5 duplex et possèdent tous un balcon ou une terrasse. Certains logements en RDC possèdent aussi des jardins privatifs. Le bâtiment A23 est scindé en deux volumes liés par des passerelles et est en R+2+Combles Une crèche et deux locaux associatifs seront livrés brut au RDC du bâtiment A23. Dans le cadre du présent marché, l’attention de l’ENTREPRENEUR est attirée sur le fait que l’opération vise une labellisation RE2020 pour les 2 îlots, ainsi qu’une certification NF Habitat HQE, uniquement pour l’îlot A1.

title: Netherlands – Repair and maintenance services – EA Technisch onderhoud
description: Het realiseren van een veilige, betrouwbare, duurzame en toekomstbestendige technische exploitatie van het EYE Filmmuseum, waarbij de gebouwgebonden installaties optimaal bijdragen aan de continuïteit van de bedrijfsvoering en de bezoekersbeleving. De geraamde opdrachtwaarde bedraagt € 3.100.000 exclusief btw over de maximale looptijd van tien (10) jaar, inclusief optiejaren. Deze raming is opgebouwd uit twee onderdelen: 1. Publieksgebouw (EYE Filmmuseum) De raming is gebaseerd op de huidige jaarlijkse uitgaven van circa € 100.000 exclusief btw voor technisch onderhoud en € 80.000 exclusief btw voor reparaties, vervangingen en onderdelen, totaal € 180.000 per jaar. Over een periode van tien jaar bedraagt dit € 1.800.000. Op dit bedrag is een opslag toegepast voor prijsontwikkelingen, indexering en een toenemende onderhoudsbehoefte als gevolg van veroudering van gebouw en installaties. 2. Aanvullend (optioneel) - Collectiecentrum Voor het mogelijke toe te voegen gebouw wordt uitgegaan van jaarlijkse kosten van circa € 45.000 exclusief btw voor onderhoud en € 20.000 exclusief btw voor reparaties, vervangingen en onderdelen, totaal € 65.000 per jaar. Over tien jaar bedraagt dit € 650.000. Inclusief een opslag voor onvoorziene kosten, indexatie en ontwikkeling van de onderhoudsbehoefte. Aan deze raming kunnen geen rechten worden ontleend.

title: C1DA--674-19-101 Replace Boilers and Boiler Plant (CPS Only)
description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE The Department of Veterans Affairs, Network Contracting Office (NCO) 17, intends to award a sole source, Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract to Cox Design Associates, Inc., a certified Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB). The requirement is to provide Architect/Engineer (A/E) Construction Period Services (CPS) for Project 674 19 101, Replace Boilers and Boiler Plant, located at the Temple VA Medical Center, 1901 Veterans Memorial Drive, Temple, TX 76504. The applicable NAICS code is 541310 Architectural Services, with a size standard of $12.5M. Cox Design Associates, Inc. previously completed the 100% design and construction documents for this project under a separate A/E contract. Construction is active, and the VA now requires continued CPS throughout the remaining construction period to ensure proper interpretation, adjustment, and execution of the original design intent. The required CPS includes but is not limited to: Construction submittal reviews; Responses to Requests for Information (RFIs); Preparation of supplemental instructions and design clarifications; Review of potential change orders; Attendance at site visits and weekly construction meetings; Oversight ensuring the Designer of Record (DOR) design is executed accurately. Cox Design Associates, Inc. possesses unique design knowledge and remains the Designer of Record (DOR). Any firm proposing to take over CPS responsibilities must demonstrate in writing how it would effectively and efficiently assume full responsibility for interpreting and administering another firm s design, including: Detailed knowledge of the design rationale, engineering decisions, and analysis, Ability to perform CPS within the same technical footprint as the DOR, Willingness to assume full liability for design interpretation, corrections, or changes that may arise during construction. Any prospective A/E firm asserting capability to meet this requirement may give a written notification to the Contracting Officer in the form of a capability statement, including an explanation of how the contractor would be able to effectively and efficiently operate in the same footprint as the A/E DOR. This procurement will be conducted under the authority of 41 USC §3304(a)(5), 38 U.S. Code § 8127(c), as implemented by RFO 6.103-5 (Authorized or Required by Statute). The requirement will be awarded using the non-competitive (sole-source) procedures authorized in VAAR 819.7008 (DEVIATION) for sole-source awards to certified SDVOSBs up to $5,000,000. A Justification & Approval (J&A) will be posted after award in accordance with FAR 6.301. THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. No responses to this notice are requested. No solicitation will be issued. If a firm believes VA should not proceed with this sole-source action, it may submit a capability statement by 10:00 AM (Central Time), October 14, 2026, to: Ms. Makarim.Abdul Jabbar@va.gov Contracting Officer, NCO 17 Telephone inquiries will not be accepted. The VA will NOT reimburse any costs associated with responding to this notice. Information received will be used solely to determine whether a competitive procurement is appropriate. A determination not to compete the proposed contract will be made at the sole discretion of the Government.

description: Federal Acquisition Service Office of Shared Service Delivery Personal Property Management FIREARMS SALES AND DISPOSAL REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) RFI # FDCB-2026-0001 NAICS: 423910 � Sporting and Recreational Goods and Supplies Merchant Wholesalers 332994 � Small Arms, Ordnance, and Ordnance Accessories Manufacturing General Services Administration 1800 F Street, NW Washington, D.C. 20405 1.0 Description The General Services Administration (GSA), Federal Acquisition Service (FAS), Office of Shared Service Delivery, Personal Property Management (PPM), is seeking information related to the sale of firearms that are no longer required for Federal mission requirements. 2.0 Firearms Sales and Disposal Background Information The Federal Government purchases billions of dollars in supplies, materials, and personal property annually and must efficiently dispose of unneeded personal property on a continuous basis. The Personal Property Program within GSA oversees the reuse, donation, and sale of Federal personal property in an effective and efficient manner. Federal customers utilize PPM to dispose of excess and surplus property, as well as exchange/sale property, seized and forfeited property, and other categories of personal property. The reuse of personal property assets within the Government saves taxpayer funds, while donation of property to eligible recipients ensures that assets no longer required by the Government continue to benefit the public in communities across the country. When property is sold, sales proceeds may be returned to customer agencies to support their missions or deposited into the U.S. Treasury, as authorized. Additionally, only warranted Sales Contracting Officers may conduct sales of Federal property and award sales contracts to buyers. The Government intends to begin selling unneeded Federal firearms in order to recoup the Government�s investment in these assets when they are no longer required for Federal mission requirements. The Government anticipates selling firearms to Federal Firearms License holders (FFLs), including Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs), through negotiated sales or by establishing term sales contracts. Such firearms are classified under Federal Supply Class (FSC) 1005, Guns, through 30mm. FFLs are businesses engaged in the dealing or manufacture of firearms and are licensed by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) pursuant to 18 U.S.C. � 923. The purpose of this RFI is to ascertain the capabilities of FFLs, including OEMs, that may be interested in purchasing unneeded Federal firearms or providing services related to the disposal of such firearms. 3.0 Requested Information: Industry Questions for Industry: How do you determine the fair market value of previously used firearms? What information should the Government provide about each firearm to allow industry to determine fair market value, market interest, and lawful disposition options? How important is physical inspection before purchase? What information would be needed in place of a physical inspection? What types of firearms do you purchase? Are there any types of firearms you will not purchase? If so, why? Do you purchase firearms covered by the National Firearms Act (NFA)? Do you offer shipping and transportation services from firearms sellers, including the Government? If so, how do you coordinate shipping? Do you have the ability to coordinate shipping from a variety of disparate locations and entities across the continental United States, Alaska, Hawaii, the District of Columbia, and U.S. territories? Do you bear the shipping costs? If so, do you invoice shipping costs separately or reduce fair market value reimbursements to offset shipping costs? Are there minimum quantity requirements for shipping services? What standard practices are used for transportation, pickup, receipt, and chain-of-custody documentation when firearms are transferred from Government or law enforcement sellers? Do you have experience purchasing firearms from Government or law enforcement agencies? What transaction structures are commonly used for sales of Government or law enforcement firearms, such as lot sales, negotiated sales, auctions, term sales contracts, OEM buybacks, or a combination? What legal, regulatory, licensing, transfer, or documentation requirements should the Government consider when selling or disposing of Federal firearms to Federal Firearms Licensees? Do you have experience purchasing firearms derived from seizure or forfeiture? Do you have experience purchasing firearms that are considered historical or collectible? How do you determine the value of historical or collectible firearms? Do you purchase unexpended ammunition? How do you determine the market value of ammunition? Are there minimum quantity requirements? 4.0 Responses 4.1 Responses to this RFI are due by 10:00 a.m. Central Time (CT) on October 14, 2026, and must be submitted using the following form: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSf38agmRbJOPy-GR1Yp0wN1JleqZiZLPJR7eFT2gRtsY2IUcw/viewform?usp=dialog 4.2 Section 1 of the response shall provide administrative information and shall include the following: 4.2.1 Name, mailing address, phone number, and email address of the designated point of contact. 4.2.2 Business type (large business, small business, etc.) based upon the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code(s) identified by the respondent. title: Fort Sill Chemical Latrines BPA
description: This is a Sources Sought to establish a Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA). This BPA will be established in order to facilitate support and provide multiple permanent chemical-type latrine rentals and daily to weekly services as requested at specified locations for all units on Fort Sill, Oklahoma. 1. The Contractor shall provide latrines, handwashing stations, and all maintenance and repairs to maintain neat, clean, and sanitary conditions. This includes toilet paper (at least two rolls), paper towels, soap, and hand sanitizer. 2. The Contractor shall exchange the latrines and/or handwashing stations as required due to age and condition, or maintenance and repair requirements, to maintain neat, clean, and sanitary conditions. Replacement of chemical latrines and handwashing stations shall be recommended to the Ordering Official (OO), and approval received from the Ordering Official, prior to replacement to minimize arbitrarily expending funds on replacement costs. 3. The Contractor shall clean and service the chemical latrines and handwashing stations while units are in place per pricing schedule located in the BPA agreement. If additional service is required, it will be requested on an individual basis. 4. The Contractor shall furnish referenced supplies (portable latrines, handwashing stations, toilet paper, paper towels, soap, and hand sanitizer) and services, if and when requested by the Contracting Officer (KO), or his/her authorized representative, during the period specified herein. 5. When more than one unit is positioned at any location, the Contractor shall place the units as close together as feasible for user convenience and organized appearance. The Contractor shall ensure all units are secured in case of windy inclement weather. The Contractor shall furnish replacement units for all units removed for maintenance, repair or units that have toppled over. 6. Each unit shall be able to withstand wind velocity up to 75 MPH and at certain areas, may be anchored to ensure personnel safety and prevention of tipping over. Before performing the option to anchor, the Contractor will need to reach out to the Contracting Officer Representative (COR). 7. The Contractor shall notify the COR prior to replacing any chemical latrines or handwashing stations. 8. Chemical latrines shall be placed at least (10) feet off of any roads and improved trails. 9. The Contractor shall clean the inside and outside of all units to ensure that all surfaces including seats, doors, walls, floors, urinals and exterior surfaces are free of all human waste, soiled toilet articles and appear clean and disinfected. After emptying the units, the Contractor shall refill each unit with standard commercial sanitizing chemicals IAW with the manufacturer�s recommendations. The Contractor shall restock each unit with a minimum of two (2) rolls of toilet paper (or more if needed) to last until the next servicing date. Weather shall not be a factor in preventing the latrines from being maintained in a clean usable state. 10. The Contractor shall properly dispose of all waste at an of-post location. The Contractor may not dump, discharge or cause to be discharged any wastes anywhere within Fort Sill. Disposal shall be in accordance with existing local, state, and federal regulations. The Contractor shall be responsible for any permits or fees associated with the use of of-post disposal location. 11. The Contractor may be required to provide emergency delivery with less than 24 hours� notice. Calls for emergency services shall be placed to the Contractor by the Contract Officer or Contract Officer Representative. The Contractor shall respond within 4 hours. Emergency services shall be priced as a single fee per incident, not per latrine in which incident is defined as only the fee to expedite, not the price for the latrine rental, delivery, servicing etc. 12. Any damages assessed under the Chemical Latrine Blanket Purchase Agreement(s) will be reported to the Contracting officer, or the designated representative, and accompanied by pictures of damaged unit. Supplier agrees that the fixed prices quoted to the Government will be as low as or lower than those charged to the Supplier�s most favored customer for comparable quantities under similar terms and conditions, in addition to any discounts for prompt payment. 13. The Contractor shall properly dispose of all waste at an of-post location. The Contractor may not dump, discharge or cause to be discharged any wastes anywhere within Fort Sill. Disposal shall be in accordance with existing local, state, and federal regulations. The Contractor shall be responsible for any permits or fees associated with the use of of-post disposal location. 14. Contractor shall be located within a 60 Mile radius of Fort Sill, Oklahoma. The Mission and Installation Contracting Command (MICC), Fort Sill, Oklahoma, intends to award a seven-year Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) to a maximum of three local contractors (within 60- mile radius) that meet the requirement. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) Code is 562991 is applicable to the acquisition. The applicable size standard is $9 million. Call-out made against this BPA shall be made only by authorized individuals possessing a Government Purchase Card (GPC) and who are authorized by MICC, Fort Sill. All notifications received within fifteen (15) days after the date of publication of this Sources Sought will be considered by the Government. A determination by the Government to issue agreements limited to only three (3) qualified vendors located within the 60-mile radius based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the government. This Sources Sought is not a request for proposal. It is a market research tool being used to determine the number of interested vendors. The Government is not obligated to and will not pay for any information received from potential sources as a result of this Sources Sought. All responses shall include, at a minimum, the following information. Company�s full name, address, telephone number, point of contact with email address, and Federal Tax Identification Number. Company�s Unique Identification Number (UEI) and Cage Code for System for Award Management (SAM). A statement indicating the offeror�s ability to accept payment via Government Credit Card. Company Size: small or large, HUBZone, 8(a), SDB, Woman-owned, Service Disabled Veteran-Owned. Set aside criteria will be considered. Vendor Capability Statement. Any questions may be directed to Thomas Green (Contracting Officer) at thomas.m.green111.civ@army.mil and Indigo Delacruz (Contract Specialist) at indigo.a.delacruz.civ@army.mil.

title: Balfour Beatty - Roads North of the Thames - LTC - FRC Structures Package
description: The Lower Thames Crossing Roads, North Programme is seeking expressions of interest from suppliers with experience in reinforced concrete (FRC) and structural works. The scope is expected to include elements such as reinforced concrete foundations, abutments, retaining walls, pile caps, reinforced earth structures, bridge structures and other civil engineering works. As part of our procurement planning, we are considering a range of packaging options, including splitting the works into multiple packages. Through this PQQ, we are looking to better understand the market's capability, capacity and preferred delivery models to help inform the final procurement strategy. What We're Looking For We would like to hear from organisations with experience in one or more of the following: Reinforced concrete foundations Reinforced concrete abutments Reinforced concrete retaining walls Reinforced earth structures Pile caps and substructures Bridge and highway structures Structural concrete works Civil engineering and infrastructure projects Design, construction, supply and installation services Temporary works design and management Quality assurance, testing and commissioning We welcome responses from organisations of all sizes, including SMEs, either independently or as part of a consortium, joint venture or wider supply chain arrangement. How to Apply If you are interested in this opportunity, please complete the attached FRC Structures Package Eligibility Criteria Questionnaire and return it to the Supply Chain Team by 14.10.26 at: BBLTCProcurementandSupplyChain@balfourbeatty.com Please ensure all sections of the questionnaire are completed, as this will help us gain a full understanding of your organisation's capabilities, capacity and experience. The qualification questions have been designed to assess your ability to meet Balfour Beatty and Lower Thames Crossing supply chain requirements and will help inform the final packaging strategy for these works. As we are currently considering a number of packaging options, including smaller and specialist work packages, we are particularly interested in understanding the scale of work your organisation can deliver, your technical capabilities and your preferred delivery model. Additional information: The Lower Thames Crossing (LTC) is a new road to better connect Essex and Kent through a tunnel beneath the River Thames. Our purpose is to drive a change in how we deliver - connecting people to jobs and businesses to opportunities, leaving a skills legacy for the local community and construction industry, all whilst restoring nature and drawing a new blueprint for low-carbon construction. Our ambition is to deliver the UK's greenest road, and to do the right thing for local communities and the environment. We can only achieve this with the support of our supply chain, and it is therefore critical that for any supplier to be successful in winning work on LTC, they must demonstrate commitments to supporting delivery of our ambitions: • Delivering the works through a 'zero emissions' solution, and not using diesel on site in any plant or machinery. • Supporting us to leave a skills legacy for the local community, by not only recruiting locally, but upskilling your workforce to enable meaningful progression into higher paid higher skilled work. • Helping to facilitate successful opportunities by providing early careers roles, as well as inspiring young people into construction through delivery of STEM engagement.

title: Drone Killer Cartridge Training Device
description: This Special Notice is to advisr intrested memebers of the Training and REadiness Accelerator II (TREII), as well as other intrested memebers within the U.S technology base, that a Request for Solutions (RFS) has been issued by Advanced Technology International (ATI) to develop a training device of the Drone Killer Cartridge. The device needs to reasonably replicate the effects of the 5.56mm and 7.62mm ammunition against Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS ) in Force on Force training. The device must work with the soldier�s issued weapon. The purpose the the Training and Readiness Accelerator II ( TREXII) is to spur innovative development, demostration, and expedited delivery of prototypes to increase Warfighter readiness via modeling, simulation, education/ training, expermental validation , and miltary readinesss focused projects, A constorium has been estabblished to develop prototypes directly relevant to enhancing th emission effectiveness to develop prototypes personnel and the supporting the platforms, systems, components, or materials proposed to be acquired or developed by the Department of Defense (DoD), or to improvement of platforms, systems, components of materials in use by the Armed Forces. Link for TREX Il-https://www.trexii.org/ Desired Objectives: STE LTS requires a training device to simulate the Drone Killer Cartridge in Force on Force training. The Drone Killer Cartridge will engage training UASs in a non-destructive method. The training device must have a range of at least 125 meters but the range must not exceed 150 meters. The training device must have an effects circle of 3 meters at 125 meters. As a soldier can fire either the Drone Killer Cartridge or standard 5.56 ball ammunition, the device must replicate both capabilities. For 5.56 ball, the device must meet current Individual Weapon System (IWS) capabilities. Size, weight and battery life are key considerations in selecting the prototype(s). This Request for Solution seeks to develop a training device of the Drone Killer Cartridge. The device needs to reasonably replicate the effects of the 5.56mm and 7.62mm ammunition against Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS ) in Force on Force training. title: Z1DA--VANJHCS Demolition and Abatement IDIQ East Orange and Lyons
description: General Information 2.1 Location Work performed under this scope shall be for and conducted within the VA New Jersey Health Care System (VANJHCS) at the East Orange VA Medical Center, located at 385 Tremont Ave, East Orange, NJ 07018, and Lyons VA Medical Center, located at 151 Knollcroft Rd, Lyons NJ 07939. 2.2 Purpose This Statement of Work (SOW) is for an IDC for demolition and abatement efforts supporting construction and repair services at VANJHCS Medical Centers. These services shall be provided on an as needed basis, for a five-year term. VANJHCS has various sized projects that require a Contractor to perform the demolition and abatement portion of this work necessary to accomplish this goal. The minimum value for this IDC is $10,000.00 with a maximum dollar value of $2,000,000.00. 2.3 Scope A description of all individual demolition and abatement tasks covered under this IDC contract can be found in the contract Line Items. The contractor shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, tools, transportation, supervision, safety, quality control and management necessary to fulfill the requirements of task orders issued by the Government under this contract. All work completed under this contract shall comply with applicable Infection Control requirements and the New Jersey Administrative CodeA (NJAC) 5:23-8, Asbestos Hazard Abatement Subcode, and NJAC 12:120 governing asbestos abatement, licensing, and permitting requirements. Additional administrative and management related requirements are described in Section 3: Requirements. Material testing and air monitoring services required while performing asbestos removal services shall be provided by the VANJHCS at no cost to the contractor. No work outside the defined Statement of Work (SOW) shall be performed without written authorization from the Contracting Officer (CO). Unauthorized work may be deemed Unauthorized Commitment (UAC) and may not be reimbursed. The Contractor shall be responsible for all means and methods and shall ensure all work is performed in a safe, compliant, and professional manner.

FAR 52.228-1 Bid Bond/Offer Guarantee: A bid bond/offer guarantee shall be submitted at time of offer on a Standard Form 24 (SF24), Failure to provide the bid bond will render the offer non-responsive, resulting in its rejection. The required guarantee amount is 20% of the total offer price, not to exceed a maximum of $3 million. Alternative Payment Protections FAR 52.228-13 (July 2000) (a) The Contractor shall submit the following payment protections: Payment Bonds (b) The amount of the payment protection shall be 100% of the contract price. (c) The submission of the payment protection is required within 10 days of contract award. (d) The payment protection shall provide protection for the full contract performance period plus a one-year period. (e) Except for escrow agreements and payment bonds, which provide their own protection procedures, the Contracting Officer is authorized to access funds under the payment protection when it has been alleged in writing by a supplier of labor or material that a nonpayment has occurred, and to withhold such funds pending resolution by administrative or judicial proceedings or mutual agreement of the parties. (f) When a tripartite escrow agreement is used, the Contractor shall utilize only suppliers of labor and material that signed the escrow agreement. (End of clause) Payment Bond must be submitted using the mandatory Standard Form (SF) 25A. Please note that no substitute forms will be accepted. Payment Bonds are due no later than 10 calendar days after award and must be submitted to Contract Specialist, Holly Hlavac via email at Holly.Hlavac@usda.gov and Contracting Officer, Lucas Dahlman at Lucas.Dahlman@usda.gov before work begins.

description: This is the synopsis associated with Sources Sought Notice. This synopsis for the annual bulk fuel procurement for the Atlantic/Europe/Mediterranean (AEM) Purchase Program 2027. Delivery modes will be by tanker and pipeline. FOB Destination tanker offers will not be accepted. The requirements may increase during the delivery period and be met by supplemental solicitations tied to this procurement. The Tentative requirement details for this procurement are: The Total Estimated Quantities are as follows: Turbine Fuel, Aviation (JA1); NSN: 9130-00-753-5026, 201,690,000 USG Turbine Fuel, Aviation (JP5); NSN: 9130-00-273-2379, 41,277,000 USG Turbine Fuel, Aviation (JP8); NSN: 9130-01-031-5816, 9,111,000 USG Fuel, Naval Distillate (F76); NSN: 9140-00-273-2377, 64,911,000 USG Ordering and Delivery Period: Under Purchase Programs 1.1b, 1.1d and 1.1i the Ordering Period is date of award through June 30, 2028. The Delivery Period is July 1, 2027, through June 30, 2028, with a 30-day Carry Over period. The 30-day carryover period allows for delivery of orders placed prior to the end of the ordering period. Period of Performance: One year Place of Performance: Atlantic/Europe/Mediterranean locations Solicitation Availability: This solicitation will be available on the World Wide Web https://www.sam.gov. Please be advised that a hard copy of the solicitation will not be available. DLA Energy will be using the Bulk Offer Entry Tool (OET) for this Procurement. The usage of the Bulk OET is mandatory. The Bulk OET will allow Offerors to electronically submit and sign their offer (including the SF1449). If you intend to submit an offer, please familiarize yourself with the system and its requirements ahead of time. A user manual for Bulk Fuels OET can be found at: https://oet.energy.dla.mil/bulkoet/BulkOETServlet?class=umanmethods&method=getUM The items under this acquisition may be subject to an Agreement on Government Procurement approved and implemented in the United States by the Trade Agreement Act of 1979. All offers shall be in the English language and in U.S. dollars. The quantity contemplated is 22,000,000U.S. gallons (USG) of F76 delivered by Pipeline, for Defense Fuel Supply Point (DFSP) Rota, located in Rota, Spain for the same delivery period as the rest of the requirements. Moeve is specified as the only source authorized to supply this fuel requirement within Spain. All responsible sources may submit a bid, proposal, which shall be considered by the agency. Authorization from Moeve to access the Moeve Refinery pipeline that can deliver F76 to the DFSP Rota storage tanks must be included. This is not a request for competitive proposals. Other interested parties may submit a capability statement which shall be considered by the Government. The capability statement must include authorization from Moeve to supply this requirement. title: Building 215 Clean Room HEPA Filter Replacement
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) BUILDING 215 ADVANCED MEASUREMENT LABORATORY (AML) CLEANROOM REPAIR AND HEPA FILTER REPLACEMENT Solicitation/Reference No.: 1333ND26RNB190014 1. PURPOSE OF THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) is conducting market research pursuant to Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 10 and FAR 15.201 to obtain industry feedback concerning the scope, schedule, phasing, cleanroom outage requirements, technical and performance risks, and estimated construction cost associated with the Building 215 Advanced Measurement Laboratory (AML) Cleanroom Repair and HEPA Filter Replacement project. NIST previously solicited this requirement under Solicitation No. 1333ND26RNB190014. NIST did not receive an acceptable offer under that solicitation. NIST is therefore reassessing the requirement and acquisition approach before determining whether and how to resolicit the project. NIST is particularly interested in identifying aspects of the requirement that may materially affect industry participation, constructability, schedule feasibility, pricing, risk, or the ability of contractors to submit competitive proposals. Industry is encouraged to provide candid feedback and to identify recommended changes that could improve constructability, competition, schedule feasibility, cost certainty, and overall project execution while continuing to meet NIST�s mission and cleanroom operational requirements. 2. RFI / MARKET RESEARCH NOTICE THIS RFI IS ISSUED SOLELY FOR INFORMATION AND ACQUISITION PLANNING PURPOSES. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP), INVITATION FOR BID (IFB), REQUEST FOR QUOTATION (RFQ), OR OTHER SOLICITATION. The Government does not intend to award a contract based on responses to this RFI. Responses will be treated as information only and shall not be construed as offers or proposals that can be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government will not reimburse respondents for costs incurred in preparing or submitting information in response to this RFI or for participating in any follow-up discussions. This RFI does not obligate the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract, nor does it restrict the Government�s ultimate acquisition approach. Respondents are advised that information submitted in response to this RFI may be used by NIST in developing or revising the acquisition strategy, statement of work, specifications, schedule, phasing requirements, outage requirements, Government cost estimate, and future solicitation. Respondents should clearly identify and mark any proprietary, confidential, or commercially sensitive information contained in their responses. Respondents should avoid including proprietary information unless necessary to provide a meaningful response. 3. PROJECT BACKGROUND The project involves repair and modernization work within the Building 215 Advanced Measurement Laboratory cleanroom located at the NIST Gaithersburg Campus. The AML cleanroom encompasses approximately 1,800 square meters and includes approximately 750 square meters of Class 100 cleanroom space. The facility supports sensitive NIST research activities and contains specialized and, in some instances, irreplaceable scientific equipment. description: CONTINGENCY OPERATIONS OF JOB CORPS CENTERS NATIONWIDE On or about October 2026, the US Department of Labor (DOL), Office of the Assistant Secretary for Administration and Management (OASAM), Office of the Senior Procurement Executive (OSPE), Job Corps Acquisition Services (JCAS) anticipates issuing a Request for Proposal, (RFP), for Contingency Operations of Job Corps Centers nationwide. The RFP will be posted as a multiple award indefinite delivery/indefinite quantity (IDIQ) contract with 8 full and open awards and 4 awards set-aside exclusively for small business. The Job Corps program was originally established by the Economic Opportunity Act of 1964; current authorization for the program is authorized under the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA) of 2014. The Job Corps program is a national residential and non-residential training and employment program administered by the US Department of Labor to address multiple barriers to employment faced by disadvantaged youth, ages 16-24 years, throughout the United States. This requirement is for the establishment of multiple Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contracts, under which Fixed Price Task Orders will be placed in the event Job Corps requires a short-term contingency operator for any Job Corps Center located within the United States or its territories. The operation of the Job Corps Center would include providing academic, career technical, career success skills, and career development training, and related support services. The Contractor shall also provide Outreach and Admissions services for residential male and female students, and nonresidential male and female students. The Contractor shall undertake all measures and efforts necessary to ensure that the center attains and/or maintains an average monthly OBS equal to 100% of the center�s planned OBS. Further, the Contractor shall provide Career Transition Services for all graduates of the center, regardless of where the graduate or former enrollee resides or matriculates. title: NAWCAD WOLF SPN-50 Presolicitation Notice
description: INTRODUCTION The NAWCAD WOLF ATC&LS Division, operating under the organic Lead Systems Integrator� (oLSI�) model, has requirements for services and hardware for the overhaul support, field support, depot management support, logistics support, inventory and failure data reporting support, software analysis and troubleshooting support, engineering change proposal support, engineering and technical support, system installation and integration support, and program management support of the AN/SPN-50(V) Shipboard Air Traffic Radar. Detailed specifications for the services and hardware to be furnished by the Contractor shall be set forth in an individual Task Order (TO) awarded under the Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA). The BOA requirement is in direct support of projects related to multiple major defense acquisition programs, other acquisition category designations, and/or other defense weapons systems to include, but not be limited to, AN/SPN-50(V) with an agile management approach to ensure that solutions are delivered efficiently and effectively. The TO will provide overhaul support, field support, material support, logistics support, inventory and failure data reporting support, software and cyber analysis and troubleshooting support, software Engineering Change Proposal (ECP) support, hardware and obsolescence ECP support, engineering and technical support, and program management support. The Government intends to negotiate and establish a Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) with Saab, Inc., East Syracuse, New York, and to issue an initial task order under that BOA for the requirements described in this notice. This acquisition is intended to be pursued on a sole source basis under Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.103-1, "Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements." A determination by the Government not to compete this effort is solely within the discretion of the Government. This notice is issued for informational and market-research purposes under FAR Part 10. It is not a solicitation, request for proposal, or request for competitive quotations, and it does not constitute a commitment by the Government to award a contract, establish a BOA, or issue an order. The Government is seeking capability statements from interested sources to assess whether any other responsible source can satisfy the stated requirements. Responses will be considered solely for that purpose. If the information received demonstrates that another responsible source can meet the Government�s requirements, the Government may revise its acquisition approach. Absent such information, the Government intends to proceed with the anticipated sole-source BOA and initial task order to Saab, Inc. Responses to this notice are not offers and will not be treated as proposals. DISCLAIMER THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. PROGRAM BACKGROUND The function of the AN/SPN-50(V) Shipboard Air Traffic Radar is to enable Air Traffic Controllers the ability to provide radar Air Traffic Control (ATC) services to joint-coalition forces across the full range of military operations, such as aircraft sequencing and separation, airspace identification and containment, safety alerts, and traffic advisories in all weather conditions. This requirement is a subsequent procurement associated with contract N0019-23-C-0049 and will assume a limited portion of the tasking transitioning from that contract. Contract N0019-23-C-0049 is a Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR) Low-Rate Initial Production (LRIP) interim sustainment contract. Upon completion of the applicable LRIP effort, the Air Traffic Control and Landing Systems (ATC&LS) Division, in its capacity as the official In-Service Engineering Agent (ISEA) for the AN/SPN-50(V), will be responsible for sustaining the system. The Government anticipates establishing a sole-source Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) under which service Task Orders (TOs) and hardware Delivery Orders (DOs) may be issued. The resultant BOA is anticipated to include a five-year ordering period. Service TOs are anticipated to include Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF) term and Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Contract Line Item Numbers (CLINs) for labor, as well as cost-reimbursement CLINs for Other Direct Costs (ODCs). Hardware DOs are anticipated to use FFP CLINs. The anticipated award date for the BOA and initial TO is March 2027, with an anticipated period of performance from March 2027 through March 2032. These dates are subject to change. REQUIRED CAPABILITIES To be considered capable, a Contractor must: Demonstrate extensive experience in providing full lifecycle support for complex radar or avionics systems. This includes overhaul, restoration, and repair in accordance with MIL-STD-2110; field support for troubleshooting and operational analysis; and robust engineering support encompassing anomaly investigation, root cause analysis, and the development of Engineering Change Proposals (ECPs) for hardware, software, and obsolescence issues. Possess a proven capability in managing the entire logistics and supply chain process. This includes establishing and executing a proactive Diminishing Manufacturing Sources and Material Shortages (DMSMS) Management Program, maintaining a counterfeit electronic part detection and avoidance system compliant with SAE AS5553 and AS6174, and managing provisioning and technical data (LPD, PTD, TDP) in accordance with SAE GEIA-STD-0007C. Have the ability to manage and sustain the SPN-50(V) Air Traffic Radar system's software and cybersecurity posture. This requires providing software and cyber analysis, implementing fixes for defects and vulnerabilities, delivering Configuration Managed (CM) software builds, and maintaining a Cybersecurity Implementation Plan (CSIP) that aligns with the government's Cybersecurity Plan (CSP). Have an established Higher-Level Quality Management System (QMS) certified to ISO 9001:2015 or equivalent, with workmanship meeting IPC Class 3 standards for high-performance electronics. Demonstrate strong program management capabilities to coordinate all cost, schedule, and technical aspects of the SOW, including the management of subcontractors and the ability to support travel (CONUS and OCONUS) on short notice. A draft Statement of Work (SOW) and draft CDRLs are attached for review. ELIGIBILITY The applicable North American Industry Classification (NAICS) code for this requirement is 541330 � Exception A - Military and Aerospace Equipment and Military Weapons and Maintenance, Repair, and Rebuilding of Equipment- Aircraft Launching, Landing, and Ground Handling Equipment. The product service code (PSC) is J017. Offerors MUST have an adequate accounting system in accordance with FAR 16.301-3(a)(3) in order to be eligible for award of this cost-type contract. SUBMISSION DETAILS Interested vendors should submit their capabilities statement in a document of no more than four (4) pages in length in Times New Roman font containing no smaller than ten-point font. This document shall demonstrate the capability to meet the required capabilities noted in this posting, including specifically addressing each of the capabilities in items a-e above. Additionally, all responses shall include Company Name, CAGE Code, Address, Business Size, and Points-of-Contact (POCs) including name, phone number, fax number and mailing address. All responses and questions for this Sources Sought shall be submitted electronically via email to Sabrina Barnes at sabrina.n.bar

This requirement will be processed under the authority 10 U.S.C.2304(c)(1), only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. As such, we recommend a sole-source, firm-fixed price procurement to Allied Defense Industries, CAGE: 0GD25.
